main_text.p: Hic est, si nescis, qui iam tibi, Roma, parauit Excidium, pestem, funera, bella, famem.
Hic est, per quem tot prostant & in urbe puellæ, Per quem pulsus honos, virgineumq; decus.
Hic est, qui molles eucxit ad astra cinædos, Formosum à tergo munere iuuit Hylam.
Hic est, qui fuerat unus infamia mundi, Imperij labes, spurcities q; sui.
Contemptor diuum, sceleru[?]m uir, publicum hostis, Perfidus, ingratus, raptor, iniquus, atrox.
Exosus uitam, & morbo tenuatus amaro, Stabat Paeonia non reuocandus ope.
Mortem implorabat, nec mortem fata finebant, Gaudebant longa sed cruciare mora.
Hic uidit mortis centum tormenta futura, Poena tamen mortis non fuit aequa suae.
Ex ista tandem migrauit luce tyrannus, Quo nullus toto peior in orbe fuit.
Roma uale, uidi, satis est uidisse: reuertar, Quum leno, aut meretrix, scurra, cinædus erat.

p.i: Sub prædicto Clemente pontifice claruisse dicitur Nicolaus Machiauellus, historicus & secretarius Florentinus. Qui in historia sua clarè ostendit, ex ambitione pontificum pleraque Christianorum prouenisse mala. Ante Theodoritum Longobardorum

page.notes: Ink underlines and strokes over several verse lines and the first line of the prose are manuscript marks, not print, and are left out. Faint marks in the left and right margins are not legible. Doubtful readings: "sceleru[?]m" in the line "Contemptor diuum, sceleru[?]m uir" is written "scelerum" in the scan, and the page number "300" is printed as an ornamented figure that is hard to read. The verse "Hic est, si nescis" is printed with "nescis" as shown.
